title: Prototype Building
searchIntent: grok bot to build a prototype
intro: Prototype work is mostly unglamorous: turning a decision you have already made into something running, then leaving it somewhere a colleague can click on it. That shape suits a Bot better than open-ended engineering does, because the hard part has already been settled before the work starts. The bots below take a written brief and produce a working artefact from it. What separates them is how much they assume — some expect a specification tight enough to implement without asking, others will make product decisions on your behalf, which is usually the failure mode you want to avoid. Where a bot runs on a schedule rather than on demand, that is noted, since an unattended agent opening pull requests overnight needs a review step you actually honour.

bots.fitReason: Purpose-built one-shot prototyping: hand it a brief for a chat app, directory, todo or game and it ships Vite + React + TypeScript on a Convex backend. Scope is fixed to that stack, so it is no use if the prototype has to live in your existing codebase.

Takes a product brief to a working Convex + TanStack + React build with UI that does not look like a wireframe, which is what a clickable prototype needs. It will exercise design judgement on your behalf, so come with the decisions already made if you want them respected.

You state what to build and the check that proves it done, and it keeps a coding agent grinding on your machine until that check passes. Only as good as your definition of done — a vague brief here produces a loop, not a prototype.

Runs the actual Grok Build CLI on an agent computer for app and code work at maximum effort, so the prototype gets built off your laptop. It is a harness rather than a product thinker: it implements the spec you give it and nothing more.

Drives Claude Code on Opus for frontend, UI and architecture work and reports a PR when the CLI exits. Geared to PR-shaped work in a repo rather than standing up a throwaway demo from nothing, and you still have to review and merge.

Local-only cursor-agent runner explicitly framed for experiments and scratch builds, which is the right posture for a prototype. Deliberately does not touch GitHub PRs, so there is no cloud artefact to hand a colleague unless you deploy it yourself.

A plain wrapper that routes all software work through the Claude Code CLI, which will build a prototype from a tight brief. No prototyping opinion of its own — it is a pipe to Anthropic's agent, so the quality of the spec is the whole game.
